candidates.title: Plcg2 Deficiency Leads to Sex-Associated Divergent Effects on Glial Transcriptomes.
candidates.abstract: Plcg2 encodes an intracellular phospholipase C signaling enzyme expressed predominately in microglia in the brain. Genome-wide association studies implicate PLCG2 in Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk and loss of Plcg2 alters amyloid pathology in mouse models. However, the physiological impact of Plcg2 loss remains unclear. To address this gap, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of wild-type, heterozygous, and homozygous Plcg2-deficient mouse brains in the absence of amyloid or tau pathology. Our analyses generated a comprehensive, publicly available atlas of glial transcriptomic states across genotypes and sexes. Genotype-associated changes in microglia and astrocytes were enriched in neurodegenerative disease-related pathways, as well as oxidative phosphorylation and proteostasis pathways. Genotype-by-sex interaction and sex-stratified analyses revealed divergent regulation of many of these pathways in males and females, while co-expression and cell-cell communication analyses identified additional sex-associated differences in glial signaling networks. Overall, these data provide a framework for understanding how variation in PLCG2 function may shape glial biology and modify pathways relevant to neurodegenerative disease in a sex-associated manner.

candidates.title: Reliability of a Two‐Stage Continuous Weighted K ‐out‐of‐ N System Based on the Residual Weight Rate Function
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT To evaluate the reliability of stochastic degradation systems, this study proposes a weighted ‐out‐of‐ hierarchical system composed of ‐out‐of‐ subsystems for . The ‐th subsystem is assembled from components, and each component exhibits two‐stage continuous weighting characteristics modeled by a newly defined residual weight rate function (RWRF). First, we establish the RWRF, which integrates component degradation quantity, service lifetime, and time‐varying weight into a unified modeling framework. Second, we formulate a weighted ‐out‐of‐ hierarchical system with multi‐type two‐stage weighted components and derive its corresponding reliability evaluation formula. Finally, by embedding the Wiener degradation process into the Weibull‐based two‐stage failure interference model, we perform theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to evaluate the performance of the proposed model.

candidates.title: Enforcing continuous symmetry in physics-informed neural networks for solving the 1D wave equation
candidates.abstract: Abstract As a typical application of deep learning, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) have gained significant attention in recent years as a mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) under the paradigm of artificial intelligence for Science. However, improving their limited accuracy remains a major challenge for PINN. Symmetry-enhanced Physics-Informed Neural Networks (SPINN) embed the invariant surface conditions derived from the Lie symmetries of PDEs into the loss function of PINN, so as to improve the solution accuracy of PDEs. This paper is the first to extend SPINN to solve the 1D wave equation, and conducts a comparative analysis with PINN. Numerical experiments show that SPINN can effectively solve the 1D wave equation. Compared with the PINN method, SPINN demonstrates better performance and effectiveness, with its predictive accuracy improved by one to two orders of magnitude, exhibiting superior predictive precision and generalization capability.

candidates.title: Quantifying the Implied Monetary Value of Specific 2-BDR Residential Property Attributes using Hedonic Pricing Model in Uyo Metropolis
candidates.abstract: This study measures the implied monetary value of structural, locational, and environmental attributes for 2-BDR residential properties in Uyo Metropolis, addressing a critical practical gap in local real estate valuation. Utilizing a crosssectional design and stratified random sampling of 387 households, the study employed Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), a disaggregated Hedonic Pricing Model (HPM), and Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM). Unlike constrained single-index models, the fully specified hedonic regression established that structural, locational, and environmental attributes collectively account for 71.4% (𝑹 𝟐 = 𝟎. 𝟕𝟏𝟒, 𝒑

candidates.title: Effectiveness of Transformer-Based Models for Detecting Depression-Related Language in Social Media: A Comparative Analysis.
candidates.abstract: Depression is one of the most common mental health conditions worldwide, yet many affected people remain undiagnosed and untreated. Social media posts provide observable language patterns associated with depression, creating an opportunity for scalable screening, but most automated approaches classify single posts in isolation and ignore the user's posting history. The purpose of this study was therefore to examine the effectiveness of a context-aware transformer-based model for detecting depression-related language in social media posts. Specifically, the study evaluated a weight-shared RoBERTa dual encoder that jointly processes the current tweet and up to five prior posts by the same user, compared it with classical classifiers using term frequency–inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) features, and analysed its errors and prediction confidence. The study was anchored on transformer self-attention and transfer learning theory and supported by Beck's cognitive theory of depression and the bias–variance trade-off. A quantitative comparative experimental design based on secondary data was adopted. The publicly available Twitter Depression Dataset was cleaned through language, length and duplicate filters, yielding 7,370 tweets from 12 accounts posted between October 2012 and August 2021, and was partitioned at the user level. On the validation set, the RoBERTa model achieved an F1-score of 0.9286, above the best classical validation F1-score of 0.9080. On a held-out test set of 1,098 tweets from two accounts, it achieved an accuracy of 0.9891, precision of 0.9528, recall of 0.9352, F1-score of 0.9439 and ROC-AUC of 0.9991, compared with an F1-score of 0.8123 for logistic regression. The model misclassified 12 tweets (5 false positives and 7 false negatives) and was markedly less certain on its errors than on its correct predictions. The study concludes that context-aware transformer representations detect dataset-defined depression-related language more effectively than classical bag-of-words approaches. However, because the labels are automatically assigned and the test set contains only two accounts, the results do not establish clinical diagnoses or generalization to new users. The study recommends that such models be used only as screening aids with human review of low-confidence predictions, and that future work use clinician-verified labels, more diverse users and statistical significance testing.
candidates.journal: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR) ISSN 2959-7056 (o); 2959-7048 (p)

candidates.title: Exploring the Role of Metacognition in Science Achievement in K-16 Education: A Systematic Literature Review
candidates.abstract: Metacognition has been the focus of various research disciplines and is generally referred to as thinking about thinking. Although metacognition is considered a crucial construct in the learning process, no systematic or meta-analytic review was found related to the comprehensive examination of the role of metacognition and its associated constructs (e.g., metacognitive awareness) in the context of science achievement in K-16 education. Therefore, this study aimed to systematically analyze the empirical research on metacognition and the associated constructs with regard to science achievement in K-16 settings. Following a systematic screening and quality assessment process conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, a total of 27 peer-reviewed journal articles were included in the final analysis. The Web of Science and Scopus databases were used for this process. According to the findings of this study, metacognition was found to be most effective in increasing exam scores and academic performance, and the most-widely used measurement tools were tests and assessments. Additionally, the three components (i.e., monitoring, planning, evaluation) of metacognitive regulation were addressed together in the majority of the reviewed studies. Lastly, none of the studies was conducted with primary school students. This review emphasizes the need for more science instruction integrated with metacognition and suggests avenues for further studies.
candidates.journal: International Journal of Education in Mathematics, Science and Technology

candidates.title: Acceptance-related perceptions of ChatGPT among first-year engineering students with prior academic use
candidates.abstract: This study examined acceptance-related perceptions of ChatGPT among first-year engineering students at a Chilean university. Psychometric analyses included 206 respondents completing all 32 items; inferential analyses included 178 reporting study-related use. Drawing on an extended technology acceptance model as a descriptive framework, we analyzed perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived intelligence, perceived trust, awareness, and adoption intention in relation to gender, school sector, prior academic performance, and usage frequency. Internal consistency estimates were high, but exploratory factor analysis showed incomplete separation of the dimensions, limiting claims of construct validity. After Holm correction, no comparisons by gender, school sector, or prior academic performance remained statistically significant. More frequent use was associated with higher scores across all six dimensions. The findings provide preliminary psychometric evidence and identify usage frequency as the most consistent correlate of acceptance-related perceptions. However, the cross-sectional design does not permit conclusions about directionality, causality, or educational benefits.
candidates.journal: Eurasia Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education

candidates.title: A quinoa-associated Pantoea isolate displays salinity-responsive auxin production and promotes plant growth under salt stress
candidates.abstract: Abstract Plant-associated bacteria can promote plant growth under saline conditions, but salinity-dependent changes in bacterial physiological traits remain insufficiently understood. Here, we isolated bacteria from surface-sterilized seedlings of the quinoa Kd line and evaluated their activity under saline conditions. A quinoa-associated Pantoea isolate, strain 6PN, promoted primary root elongation and whole-plant dry weight of Arabidopsis thaliana under salt stress, whereas no significant effect was observed under non-saline conditions. Comparative analyses with reference Pantoea agglomerans strains showed that strain 6PN exhibited salinity-responsive indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) production. Genome analysis identified a putative ipdC gene and additional genes related to stress responses, nutrient acquisition, polysaccharide biosynthesis and export, flagellar biosynthesis, and chemotaxis. Phylogenomic analysis indicated that strain 6PN was genomically distinct from representative Pantoea species examined here. In an Arabidopsis trench-plate assay, GFP-labeled strain 6PN was recovered from spatially separated plant tissues at higher levels than a GFP-labeled reference strain under saline conditions. These results identify strain 6PN as a quinoa-associated Pantoea isolate with salinity-responsive IAA production and plant growth-promoting activity under defined salt-stress conditions.

candidates.title: Human Mitochondrial HVRII as an Indicator of Island Groundwater Connectivity
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study explores the use of human mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) as a potential tracer for anthropogenic inputs in confined groundwater systems, building on our previous application in urban watersheds. mtDNA represents one of the most robust sources of eukaryotic environmental DNA (eDNA) due to its multimembrane protection, high copy number per cell, and persistence in the environment, resulting in a valuable resource for both detection and when examining sequences, tracing. We investigated mtDNA transport in the groundwater of Lord Howe Island, a small shield volcano remnant and UNESCO World Heritage site, whose modest population and limited tourist load yield a tractable number of haplotypes. By targeting the hypervariable region II (HVRII) of the human mitochondrial genome, we examined the impact of local human inputs, including septic tanks, on local groundwater. Groundwater samples were collected from wells and small groundwater discharges, PCR-amplified, and analyzed via high-throughput sequencing, revealing unique haplotype frequencies that identified zones of impact. These findings were supported by Bacteroides 16S tracking, using human, bovine, and canine specific markers as well as bacterial counts and other water quality parameters. This approach demonstrates several advantages over more traditional source tracking markers, most importantly, which impacts are uniquely anthropogenic and their origin. Unlike artificial DNA tracers, mtDNA is naturally present in septic tank leach fields and is temporally unambiguous, like plant-based viral markers. Our work highlights mtDNA’s potential to help map anthropogenic inputs within groundwater, which is a tool that may be particularly valuable for island communities with limited wastewater infrastructure resources.

candidates.title: Immune evasion in Mucorales species: From stealth spores to angioinvasive hyphae
candidates.abstract: Mucormycosis is an invasive fungal infection caused by members of the order Mucorales, which employ stage- and species-specific mechanisms to evade host immunity. Resting spores of experimentally studied Rhizopus species can persist after macrophage uptake because macrophages restrict germination but do not efficiently kill all internalized resting spores. Germination is accompanied by cell-wall remodeling and increased β-glucan exposure in several experimentally examined Mucorales species; however, functional Dectin-1-dependent responses have been demonstrated most clearly in Rhizopus and its conservation across species and isolates remains incompletely defined. Studies predominantly in Rhizopus delemar identify fungal CotH proteins as ligands for host GRP78 or integrin α3β1, linking invasion to tissue-specific host pathways. Intracellular survival also varies across species: Rhizopus spores remain dormant and prevent phagosome maturation, whereas Mucor circinelloides can germinate within macrophages via stress-response and calcineurin-dependent mechanisms. Cunninghamella shows a significant resistance to neutrophil damage, while other Mucorales species suppress accumulation of nitric oxide in activated macrophages. Studies of Rhizopus reveal morphology-dependent dendritic-cell activation and Th17 polarization, and that Rhizopus-specific T cells can directly damage fungal hyphae. Whether such adaptive responses are present in other Mucorales species remains unknown. Understanding these immune evasion mechanisms could support the development of therapies focused on cytokines, adoptive T-cells, and CotH-targets.

candidates.title: Mitochondrial Phylogeny Reveals Deep Intraspecific Divergence and Fine-Scale Regional Structure in Orangutans.
candidates.abstract: Orangutans ( Pongo spp.) are a valuable model for investigating how past climatic and geological events have shaped population structure and species diversification. We reconstructed 237 complete mitochondrial genomes from whole-genome sequencing data and combined them with 50 available mitochondrial sequences, resulting in a dataset of 287 orangutans spanning the current range of Sumatran and Bornean orangutans. Among Sumatran orangutans ( P. abelii ), we identified five geographically distinct mitochondrial clades corresponding to Langkat, North Aceh, Tripa, West Leuser and Batu Ardan. These clades showed strong differentiation, indicating long-term persistence of distinct maternal lineages across the Leuser landscape. For the recently described species, P. tapanuliensis , we added 10 newly reconstructed mitogenomes, increasing representation from 3 to 13 individuals. P. tapanuliensis formed a monophyletic, deeply divergent clade, confirming strong mitochondrial differentiation and long-term isolation. In Bornean orangutans ( P. pygmaeus ), we identified seven major regional mitochondrial clades corresponding to Sarawak, Central Kalimantan, South Kalimantan, Southeast Kalimantan, East Kalimantan and the North and South Kinabatangan populations in Sabah. Within the subspecies P. p. morio , the North and South Kinabatangan, East Kalimantan and Southeast Kalimantan clades formed distinct maternal lineages, revealing substantial mitochondrial structure within the currently recognised subspecies. Our findings suggest that current geographic and taxonomic divisions may under-represent the extent of regional maternal diversity across orangutans. Female philopatry has preserved ancient mitochondrial structure across Sundaland, with its geographic distribution shaped by refugial persistence, major riverine barriers and long-term population fragmentation.

candidates.title: Inbreeding in the genomics era: comparing IBD, drift, and homozygosity-based methods in a pig breeding population.
candidates.abstract: Background The inbreeding and kinship methods can be classified into three approaches: (1) Identity-by-Descent (IBD) estimates the probability that alleles are identical by shared ancestry; (2) Drift-based methods measure deviations in allele frequencies from a base due to genetic drift; and (3) Homozygosity-based (HOM) methods estimate genome-wide homozygosity. The objective of this study was to compare the estimated inbreeding and kinship rates using those three approaches. Within each approach, different methods were investigated. The dataset consisted of purebred sires from artificial insemination centers born between 2014 and 2024, along with their relatives with genotype data, totaling 152,883 pigs. Animals were genotyped with various SNP panels and imputed to medium- and high-density panels (50 K and 660 K). Results For inbreeding estimates, correlations among IBD-based methods were high (0.88), while correlations among drift-based methods ranged from 0.74 to 0.91. Homozygosity-based estimates showed a wide range of correlations (- 0.03 to 1.00). This variability was mainly driven by low or negative correlations involving short runs of homozygosity (ROH) classes (2-4 Mb and 4-8 Mb), which showed poor agreement with longer ROH categories. Correlations between methods from different approaches were generally weak to high (- 0.09 to 0.81). Kinship estimates showed higher correlations than inbreeding estimates. Nevertheless, the same pattern was observed: correlations were consistently higher within the same approach (above 0.96) than across different approaches (above 0.70). Rates of inbreeding and kinship per generation, estimated as regression slopes across birth years and converted to a per-generation scale, were consistently higher for drift-based measures than for the other approaches. This indicates that drift-based and homozygosity-based measures are not equivalent under genomic selection. Their differences are proportional to the covariance between changes in allele frequency and initial allele frequencies. Consequently, minor alleles tend to increase in frequency more often than expected under neutrality in this pig breeding line. Conclusions Overall, the results show that different approaches to estimating inbreeding and kinship convey distinct biological information. Homozygosity-based measures yielded lower estimates than drift-based metrics, suggesting non-neutral dynamics of allele frequencies. These findings indicate that constraining inbreeding using a drift-based genomic relationship matrix within an optimum contribution selection scheme may improve the management of genetic diversity.

candidates.title: Gray bats heighten their response to social cues when navigating group flight in environments with obstacles.
candidates.abstract: Bats are fast fliers with great maneuverability. Many species sense and communicate through echolocation, relying on acoustic signals in the environment. Bats also form large colonies, which necessitates that they fly in groups. When group size increases or obstacles are in their flight paths, the acoustic space can become cluttered, posing a non-trivial challenge for navigation. How do they interact with their environment and conspecifics, and how do they balance social and environmental cues? Recent research has uncovered individual adaptations to calling and flight patterns when flying in the groups or avoiding obstacles. Studies also suggest coordination when foraging, as well as strategies used by the group to mitigate acoustic clutter. However, there has yet to be a study on how bats weigh different navigational tasks when flying in spatially complex environments. Here, we collected stereoscopic video data from a wild colony of gray bats, Myotis grisescens, navigating their usual foraging flight paths in the presence of novel obstacles. We find that bats tend to stay close to a wall, but space out when flying in groups. We develop a data-informed agent-based model which reveals that their social repulsive behavior is strengthened when challenged to navigate novel obstacles.

candidates.title: Explainable machine learning-assisted exploration of chromatin dynamics reveals chromosome-specific response to serum starvation.
candidates.abstract: Chromatin is dynamic at all length scales, influencing chromatin-based processes, such as gene expression. Even large-scale reorganization of whole chromosome territories has been reported upon specific signals, but the lack of suitable methods has prevented analysis of the underlying dynamic processes. Here, we have used CRISPR-Sirius for time-lapse imaging of chromatin loci dynamics during serum starvation. We show that chromosome 1 loci move toward the nuclear envelope during the first hour of serum starvation in a chromosome-specific manner. Machine learning-assisted exploration of acquired multiparametric data combined with the Shapley values-based explanation approach allowed us to uncover the critical features that characterize chromatin dynamics during serum starvation. This analysis reveals that although serum starvation affects overall nuclear morphology and chromatin dynamics, chromosome 1 loci display a specific response that is characterized by maintenance of dynamics in a constrained environment, and long 'jumps' at the nuclear periphery. Interestingly, the two homologous chromosomes display differential behaviors, with the more peripheral homolog being more responsive to the signal than the internal one. Overall, the presented machine learning-assisted dataset exploration helps us navigate the multidimensional data to understand the underlying dynamic processes and can be applied to a wide variety of research questions in imaging and cell biology in general.

candidates.title: Rethinking laboratory sustainability.
candidates.abstract: Green lab initiatives like My Green Lab and LEAF (Laboratory Efficiency Assessment Framework), are paving the way towards sustainable research by promoting resource efficiency, energy conservation, and waste reduction through behavioral changes. However, these initiatives focus almost exclusively on material consumption, overlooking deeper facets of scientific waste that stem from questionable research practices: the environmental cost of unnecessary or poorly designed experiments, discarded null results, unreproducible research, and distorted reporting. I argue that a more meaningful discussion of scientific sustainability must look beyond physical resource management to examine the scientific process itself; to rethink the questions we ask, the experiments we do, and how we communicate our findings. To build a truly sustainable scientific ecosystem, Green Lab initiatives must join forces with Open Science and research integrity movements to update not only the hardware, but also the software of science.

candidates.title: Winding-up of fibrin fibers as a novel mechanism of platelet-mediated fiber compaction.
candidates.abstract: This study reveals an unrecognized mechanism by which platelets retract and compact fibrin fibers. Using a newly developed 2D fiber-retraction assay, we observed a 'gearwheel' pattern of actomyosin in spread platelets with associated, extracellular fibrin patches that appear to initiate fibrin fiber attachment and rearrangement. The outcome of this process results in two morphologically different platelet populations. Spread platelets with coiled fibers around and above their pseudo-nucleus. Other, only partially spread platelets have tightly packed fibers around bulbous protrusions ('bulbs'), mirroring the architecture of platelets and adjacent fibers within a retracted clot. Thus, the observed compaction process might take place during clot retraction to reduce clot volume, stiffen the clot, and enhance wound repair. Apart from pulling on fibers like on a rope, platelets actively wrap them into compact structures, similar to balls of wool. Using a combination of 3D clot- and 2D fiber-retraction assays, expansion and electron microscopy, live imaging, and mathematical modeling, we show that platelets use an actomyosin-driven motion to loop fibrin fibers around the base of bulbs, which form when platelets get trapped between fibrin fibers during 3D clot- or 2D fiber-retraction assays. These findings complement existing models of platel-mediated fibrin retraction, offering new insight into how platelets mechanically organize fibrin fibers.

candidates.title: Diurnal rhythmicity in metabolism and salivary effector expression shapes aphid performance on host plants.
candidates.abstract: Diurnal rhythms influence insect behavior, physiology, and metabolism, optimizing their performance by adapting to daily changes in the environment. While their impact on agricultural pests has been briefly explored, our understanding of how these rhythms drive adaptive responses in pest biology and influence host colonization remains elusive. Here, we show that a notorious global aphid pest, Rhopalosiphum padi , exhibits distinct diurnal patterns in feeding behavior, with elevated honeydew excretion at night and extended phloem salivation during early nighttime. Temporal aphid transcriptome profiling reveals four diurnally rhythmic clusters, two of which peak at night, exhibiting enrichment in carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism. Beyond the established role in manipulating host responses and allowing sustained feeding, our study reveals novel evidence of cyclical fluctuations in salivary effector expression in an insect species. Silencing key effector genes, peaking in expression during the increased nighttime salivation, results in a more pronounced reduction in aphid excretion activity on host plants during the night compared to the day, a phenomenon not observed on artificial diets. A better understanding of aphid diurnal rhythms and their roles in shaping aphid performance provides a promising avenue to refine and optimize pest management, granting a strategic advantage for minimizing crop damage.

candidates.title: Adaptive sampling: information-guided selection for targeted long-read sequencing and epigenetic studies.
candidates.abstract: Adaptive sampling (AS) is a unique feature of nanopore sequencing that enables real-time enrichment or depletion of target molecules during the sequencing run based on their initial sequence information. AS provides a flexible and scalable alternative to conventional capture- and amplification-based approaches, while preserving long reads and the ability to detect epigenetic modifications of native DNA/RNA molecules. In this review, we summarize the principles of AS-based sequencing, explain the enrichment- and depletion-mode strategies and discuss factors affecting its performance. We further highlight the growing body of studies demonstrating the utility of AS across a diverse range of applications, such as metagenomic and microbiome research, structural variant characterization and discovery, studying repeat expansion disorders, integrated genetic and epigenetic profiling or transcriptome analysis. In these and other contexts, AS enables efficient allocation of sequencing capacity toward biologically relevant molecules, while accelerating data generation, which also makes it applicable to rapid molecular diagnostics and real-time genomic analyses in clinical practice. As nanopore sequencing continues to mature and become a standard analysis approach in many laboratories, AS is likely to evolve from a specialized enrichment strategy into a routine component of genomic, epigenomic, and transcriptomic workflows.

candidates.title: GEI-17-mediated SUMOylation of GDP dissociation inhibitor GDI-1 regulates apoptotic cell clearance
candidates.abstract: by Lei Yuan, Peiyao Li, Aiying Ma, Chao Li, Fuqiao Liu, Yunmin Xie, Qian Zheng, Hui Wang, Hui Xiao Apoptotic cell clearance represents the final stage of apoptosis and involves phagosome formation, maturation, and digestion. Here, we found that SUMO modifications participate in apoptotic cell clearance by influencing phagosomal degradation activity in C. elegans . The SUMO E3 ligase, GEI-17, SUMOylates GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI-1) at K270 to trigger phagosomal degradation. Upon SUMOylation, GDI-1 facilitates release of GDP-bound RAB-1, which is subsequently converted to the GTP-bound form in a manner dependent on GDI displacement factor, PRAF-3. RAB-1 conversion enables binding and translocation of RAB-7 from the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi to promote phagosome maturation and degradation activity. In the absence of GDI-1 SUMOylation, GDI-1 binds to GDP-RAB-1, sequestering it in the cytoplasm, resulting in impaired phagosomal degradation. Furthermore, we found SUMOylation of GDI1 at a conserved site plays a crucial role in efferocytosis regulation in mammals. This study defines a previously unrecognized mechanism by which SUMOylation drives apoptotic cell clearance.

candidates.title: Local feedback governs cell fate transition to drive self-organized phenotypic equilibrium in hierarchical tumors
candidates.abstract: by Emma Legait, Charlotte Rulquin, Lauranne Bouteille, Raphaël Clément, Cédric Maurange How cell-state transitions are regulated along a tumor lineage to determine its overall cellular composition remains unclear. Using a simple hierarchical tumor model in Drosophila , we show that differentiation of cancer stem cells (CSCs) into transit amplifying progenitors (TAPs) depends on the fraction of TAPs among their immediate neighbors. This relationship is captured by a local feedback transition rule that quantitatively predicts CSC transition probability. Implementing this rule in 3D growth simulations spontaneously recapitulates CSC clustering and the emergence of a stable CSC fraction within tumors. Mechanistically, the local feedback is mediated by EGFR signaling from newly produced TAPs, propagating differentiation across CSC clusters. Consistently, we show that clustering protects the CSC pool from depletion driven by surrounding TAPs, indicating that spatial architecture and lineage dynamics are tightly coupled. Together, these findings show that a local feedback governing fate transitions drives emergent spatial organization that stabilizes the stem cell fraction in hierarchical tumors.

candidates.title: Which Fruit Traits Correlate Reliably With Sugar Content, and Does This Vary With Dispersal Syndrome?
candidates.abstract: Deciding which fruits to eat, and when, is a key decisions made by frugivores, with implications for animal nutrition, seed dispersal, and other ecosystem interactions. It has long been hypothesized that fruit traits, including color, odor, and hardness, are adapted to attract different guilds of frugivores (e.g., birds versus mammals) and facilitate fruit foraging through signaling of ripeness and nutritional reward via different sensory modalities. Yet how various traits change during ripening in fruits with different putative dispersal syndromes is poorly understood. We predicted visual traits to be more correlated with changes in sugar content during ripening in a bird-consumed fruit and odor and hardness traits to be correlated with sugar content in mammal-consumed fruits. We measured color via image analysis, odor via solid-phase microextraction GC-MS, hardness via a portable mechanical tester, and sugar content using a digital refractometer in n = 100 bananas ( Musa acuminata ) and n = 160 mangoes ( Mangifera indica ), two large, climacteric fruits as models of mammal-dispersed fruits, and in n = 80 black currants ( Ribes nigrum ), a small, non-climacteric berry as a model for bird-dispersed fruit. Bananas, and to a lesser extent mangoes, tend to get softer, have higher red-green and lower blue-yellow chromaticity values, and become more odorous as they get sweeter. Currants get softer, darker, have lower red-green and higher blue-yellow chromaticity values, and become less odorous as they become sweeter. Our results suggest that some traits, such as color and odor, may vary among plant taxa with different dispersal syndromes, while other traits, such as fruit softening, may be more consistently associated with fruit ripening when they occur. We have developed a tractable framework for assessing multimodal plant cues and signals and hope this research inspires future studies of greater taxonomic diversity.

candidates.title: The Maladaptive Stress State: A Systems Framework for Chronic Disease Persistence.
candidates.abstract: Chronic degenerative diseases are traditionally explained in terms of disease-specific initiating lesions and molecular pathways. Although this approach has substantially advanced understanding of disease mechanisms, it does not fully explain why biologically diverse disorders often converge on persistent states marked by chronic inflammation, impaired repair, altered nutrient sensing, reduced adaptive flexibility, and incomplete recovery after the initiating insult subsides. This Perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS), a systems-level framework that distinguishes disease initiation from persistence. Rather than proposing a new molecular pathway, the MSS framework integrates established knowledge from geroscience, stress biology, lysosomal signaling, nutrient sensing, and systems biology. It posits that chronic disease persists when adaptive stress programs become stabilized and the capacity to exit the stress-adapted state is impaired. Within this framework, systems-level interactions sustain evolutionarily conserved adaptive responses despite partial resolution of the original stressor. The framework also generates experimentally testable predictions and outlines translational implications for assessing therapeutic recovery through restored adaptive flexibility rather than normalization of isolated molecular biomarkers. By complementing pathway-based biology with a state-based systems perspective, the MSS framework offers a biologically grounded conceptual model for investigating persistence across diverse chronic disorders.

candidates.title: Migration as a key influence on ungulate eco-evolutionary history
candidates.abstract: by Gustavo Burin Species can overcome resource limitations by migrating to more favourable areas. A new study in PLOS Biology shows that migration has an important effect on the diversification dynamics of ungulates, that likely led to changes in ecosystem functioning. Species can overcome environmental limitations by migrating to more favorable areas. This Primer explores a new study in PLOS Biology showing that this behavior has an important effect on the diversification dynamics of ungulates, which in turn likely led to changes in ecosystem properties and functioning.

candidates.title: An indirect wing steering muscle stabilizes flight by regulating wing pitch angle in Drosophila
candidates.abstract: by Han Kheng Teoh, Debojyoti Biswas, Haoru Li, Abby Leung, B. Kemper Ludlow, Samuel C. Whitehead, Erica Ehrhardt, Michael Dickinson, Tsevi Beatus, Noah J. Cowan, Itai Cohen Flapping flight is inherently unstable, requiring Drosophila to fine-tune their wing motions on a milliseconds timescale. Pioneering studies have shown that the direct steering muscles, which attach to the wing hinge, are important for generating these rapid flight reflexes. Recent connectome data, however, reveal that indirect steering muscles or tension muscles, which alter the mechanics of the thorax, receive some of the same synaptic inputs from the sensory apparatus as the direct steering muscles. This discovery suggests that the indirect steering muscles may also be important for flight control. Here, we show that the indirect tergopleural muscles indeed contribute substantially to stabilization, particularly for large pitch perturbations. We find that for small perturbations (less than 1,000 °/s), flies modulate their wing stroke amplitude to generate lift-based corrective torques, a strategy that has been previously documented. For larger perturbations, however, we observe that Drosophila engage an additional wing degree of freedom—the wing pitch angle—to leverage additional lift and drag forces during the corrective maneuver. Quasi-steady aerodynamic simulations reveal that this strategy minimizes power consumption, anaolgous to how some mammals (including humans) adjust their steady-state gaits in a near energy-optimal manner. Using optogenetics and a control theory framework, we demonstrate that the tergopleural muscle is activated by a proportional gain component of a nonlinear proportional-integral controller responsible for determining the wing pitch angle during large perturbations. A simplified torsional spring model for the wing hinge captures the changes in the wing pitch dynamics observed during correction maneuvers by using the tergopleural muscle to adjust the rest angle of the wing. These findings provide a striking example of reflex strategy selection in time-critical behaviors and underscore the vital role of indirect steering muscles in flight stabilization.

candidates.title: Dynamic functional connectivity reveals evolving neural activity states of alcohol-seeking in rats
candidates.abstract: by Yujing Zhang, Nicholas M. Timme, Mintao Liu, Christopher C. Lapish, Joaquín Goñi The brain mechanisms underlying persistent alcohol-seeking in Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) remain incompletely understood. To investigate this behavior, we characterized the temporal evolution of neural activity states in the anterior cingulate cortex of freely behaving rats performing an aversion-resistant drinking (ARD) task. Alcohol-preferring (P) rats were assessed, as they reliably exhibit ARD when alcohol is devalued with the bitter tastant quinine. P rats were compared with Wistar rats, which progress slower to ARD, as indicated by cessation of drinking following quinine devaluation. Using dynamic functional connectivity analyses of spike-train recordings, we identified latent neural states corresponding to seeking and non-seeking phases. We then integrated the latent-state decoding of neural activity with a seeking intensity model derived from the observed drinking behavior. This framework revealed that the decoded latent neural states closely tracked behavior. Furthermore, during alcohol-reinforced sessions, neural and behavioral measures of drinking or non-drinking states were strongly aligned in both strains. However, after alcohol devaluation, this alignment diverged in P rats but remained consistent in Wistars. The inability of P rats to acquire stable neural states following devaluation suggests impaired formation of latent states as a neural mechanism of ARD, offering insights into the cognitive vulnerabilities that may sustain AUD.

candidates.title: Allosteric inhibition rescues hydrocephalus caused by catalytically inactive Shp2 in mice
candidates.abstract: by Neoklis Makrides, Emily Sun, Hilal Mir, Jen-Zen Chuang, Ziyuan Jiang, Yihua Wu, Carlos Serra, John Peregrin, Qian Wang, Wellington V. Cardoso, Ching-Hwa Sung, Neel H. Shah, Xin Zhang SHP2, a protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) crucial in Ras-MAPK signaling, is associated with various human congenital diseases and cancers. Here, we show that the catalytically inactive Shp2 C459S mutation results in communicating hydrocephalus, similar to the catalytically activating Shp2 E76K and Mek1 DD mutants. Unlike previous mutants, however, Shp2 C459S/+ mutation uniquely affects ciliary development rather than neurogenesis, leading to structural abnormalities in cilia and impaired ciliary motility. Differential scanning fluorimetry suggested that SHP2 C459S , SHP2 E76K , and SHP2 C459S/E76K mutations all induce an open SHP2 conformation, but only SHP2 C459S leads to aberrant GAB1 phosphorylation in cells expressing wild-type SHP2. Consistent with this distinct signaling profile, brain ventricular tissues from Shp2 C459S/+ mice exhibit elevated GAB1 and AKT phosphorylation despite normal ERK and STAT3 activities, implicating dysregulated PI3K–AKT signaling in the pathogenesis of hydrocephalus. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of PI3K markedly rescues ciliogenesis defects and alleviates hydrocephalus in mutant mice. Furthermore, the allosteric SHP2 inhibitor SHP099 increases the thermal stability of SHP2C459S protein, consistent with a shift toward a closed state, and ameliorates hydrocephalus in Shp2 C459S/+ mice. These findings suggest that, in this engineered mouse model, Shp2 -associated hydrocephalus is driven by conformational changes rather than altered catalytic activity. Our results underscore the therapeutic potential of conformation-specific allosteric inhibitors in targeting both catalytically active and inactive SHP2 mutants.

candidates.title: E2F4 gene therapy reverses established synaptic and cognitive deficits and remodels learning-associated signaling in Alzheimer's disease mice
candidates.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes progressive synaptic dysfunction, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline, yet strategies capable of reversing established deficits remain limited. Here, we show that neuronal expression of a p38MAPK phosphorylation-resistant human E2F4 variant (hE2F4DN), delivered by adeno-associated virus, restores hippocampal long-term potentiation and memory in homozygous 5xFAD mice after functional impairment is established. Treatment also reduces amyloid-{beta} and phospho-tau pathology and prevents hippocampal neuronal loss. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses reveal remodeling of metabolic, redox, neuroimmune, synaptic-vesicle, and GSK3{beta}-associated signaling pathways. Following contextual fear conditioning, hE2F4DN-treated mice exhibit broader learning-associated synaptic proteomic signatures and distinct phosphoregulatory responses involving synaptic machinery. These findings demonstrate that E2F4 gene therapy can reverse established synaptic and cognitive deficits while preserving neuronal integrity and reshaping molecular responses to learning, identifying E2F4 phosphorylation as a potential therapeutic target for advanced AD states.

candidates.title: Magnetic nanoparticle enrichment reveals conserved nitric oxide burst responses in Arabidopsis and wheat
candidates.abstract: Rapid nitric oxide bursts are a conserved response to environmental stimuli, but their effects on cellular S-nitrosylation remain poorly understood. We developed a fluorinated magnetic nanoparticle method for rapid, efficient profiling of S-nitrosylation. Using Arabidopsis and wheat, we treated plant tissues with S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO) to simulate a rapid nitric oxide surge. The method was then employed to capture S-nitrosylation dynamics within 24 h after treatment. Our analysis revealed sequence-dependent preferences for cysteines near basic or hydrophobic residues. Proteins showing rapid S-nitrosylation increases were predominantly associated with oxidative stress responses and energy metabolism, consistent with our metabolomic data. Functional studies using wheat TaGR1 mutants identified glutathione reductase 1 as a key regulated target. Modification at a conserved cysteine site rapidly modulated cellular glutathione levels in both species. Here, we provide an analytical tool and a multi-omics resource for investigating S-nitrosylation dynamics.

candidates.title: N-Hydroxypipecolic Acid Triggers Systemic Acquired Resistance Against Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina) in Wheat
candidates.abstract: Systemic acquired resistance (SAR) represents a conserved immune strategy enabling plants to mount long-lasting, whole-plant protection following localized pathogen challenge. In Arabidopsis thaliana, SAR is orchestrated by the mobile immune regulator N-hydroxypipecolic acid (NHP); however, the extent to which NHP defines systemic immune states in polyploid crops remains unclear. Here, we establish NHP as an inducer of systemic immunity in hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum) during infection by the obligate biotrophic fungus Puccinia triticina. Local NHP application conferred robust disease suppression in distal leaves and elicited a temporally structured oxidative response characterized by a distal, biphasic reactive oxygen species (ROS) wave linking local and systemic tissues. RNA-sequencing analysis revealed that NHP induces coordinated transcriptional reprogramming, characterized by systemic activation of pattern-triggered and effector-triggered immunity pathways, WRKY-centered transcriptional networks, NPR1-associated signaling, and broad-spectrum resistance loci including Lr34. Concomitantly, targeted metabolomic profiling revealed a unique systemic accumulation of salicylic acid, salicylic acid glucoside, pipecolic acid, and NHP, without the conventional jasmonate signaling antagonism observed in eudicots. Despite this conserved immune architecture, functional analyses indicated divergence within the NHP biosynthetic pathway; while a single wheat FMO from sub-clade A2 was systemically up-regulated by NHP, the highly conserved TaSARD4 homeologs were constitutively expressed and functionally dispensable for rust resistance in planta. Notably, heterologous expression of TaSARD4-B successfully restored NHP-glucoside accumulation in an Arabidopsis sard4 mutant, confirming biochemical competence and suggesting alternative metabolic redundancies in wheat. These findings define a systems-level NHP-driven immune state in wheat and provide a conceptual framework for dissecting systemic immunity in cereals, extending SAR paradigms beyond model plant systems.

candidates.title: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
candidates.abstract: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank. Because the published benchmark did not identify its test sets, we reran GBLUP, RKHS and elastic-net models on the same splits as TabPFN-3.5. Against the best of these, TabPFN-3.5 was significantly behind on only one trait, spruce wood density, and ahead on 12 of 18, with significant gains on all three soybean traits and rice flowering time. In the soybean panel, which had the largest number of lines, its advantage was clearest. In leave-families-out cross-validation, where models were trained on some soybean families and used to predict lines from other families withheld from training, every model lost accuracy and TabPFN-3.5 performed on par with GBLUP and RKHS. That a general-purpose learner matches or exceeds decades of specialized GP models is consistent with Sutton's Bitter Lesson, which holds that methods that scale with computation eventually overtake those built on human knowledge of the domain.

candidates.title: Endogenous Osteoblast-Osteocyte-Osteoclast Signaling Enables Bone Remodeling, Drug Response, and Cancer Invasion in a Nanoscale Calcified Bone-on-a-Chip
candidates.abstract: Bone homeostasis depends on spatially orchestrated interactions among osteoclasts, osteoblasts, and osteocytes within a unique microenvironment characterized by an extracellular matrix that is mineralized on the nanoscale. Reconstructing these interactions to enable autonomous cell differentiation and tissue remodeling remains a significant challenge in faithfully modeling bone physiology and disease in-vitro. Here, we present an engineered bone-on-a-chip platform that recapitulates the spatial organization of bone-resident cells, the differentiation of immune cells into osteoclasts, and calcified tissue resorption. We demonstrate that nanoscale mineralization of cell-laden collagen hydrogels is associated with ossification- and matrix-associated transcriptional changes and an osteocyte-like phenotype in osteoblast-lineage cells, while establishing a multicellular microenvironment associated with pro-osteoclastogenic RANKL/OPG signaling and supporting osteoclastogenesis and remodeling without the need for exogenous growth factors. Mineralized niche-driven osteoclastogenesis on-a-chip supported greater osteoclast differentiation than conventional stimulation with RANKL and M-CSF and reproduced differential responses to clinically used anti-resorptive drugs. The model further supports the integration of vascular networks and reproduces features of established tumor-bone interactions, including distinct spatial distributions of different cancer types within the mineralized microenvironment. Together, the findings establish a robust, self-regulated, and versatile microphysiologic model for investigating bone remodeling, cancer-bone crosstalk, and therapeutic interventions.

candidates.title: Engineering the Lr67-associated G144R substitution by prime editing enhances leaf rust resistance in wheat
candidates.abstract: Wheat rust diseases threaten global wheat production, highlighting the need for durable sources of resistance. The Lr67-associated G144R substitution in the sugar transport protein gene TaSTP13-D1 confers broad-spectrum resistance to multiple fungal pathogens. Here, we used an enhanced prime-editing system (ePPEplus) to introduce this resistance-associated substitution into the three TaSTP13 homoeologs in hexaploid wheat. Using the wheat-compatible JWPE1 vector, we achieved editing frequencies of 84 to 92% across the A, B, and D genomes in regenerated T0 plants. Homozygous edits were recovered in all three homoeologs, including one line carrying homozygous edits across all three genomes. Disease assays showed that edited lines had reduced leaf rust severity and fungal biomass compared with susceptible controls. Notably, the line carrying edits in all three homoeologs exhibited the greatest reduction in fungal biomass. These results demonstrate the potential of prime editing to directly introduce resistance-associated alleles into wheat and provide a strategy for accelerating the development of rust-resistant cultivars.

candidates.title: Primate Saccade Rhythmicity
candidates.abstract: Rhythmic sampling is a hallmark of many sensory systems across diverse organisms. In primate vision, rapid foveating eye movements repetitively sample the visual environment at a rate of approximately 4 Hz. Yet, the observed inter-saccadic interval distributions might equally well be produced by a non-rhythmic stochastic process as by a - putatively variable- rhythmic generator. This raises the fundamental question whether primate visual sampling differs from the numerous examples of rhythmic sampling strategies exhibited across sensory modalities and species. Here, using experiments in humans, macaques, and a marmoset, as well as statistical approaches adopted from studies of temporal structure in neuronal spiking patterns, we show that primate saccade generation is unambiguously rooted in a rhythmic source. This finding was remarkably consistent across the three primate species despite their significant evolutionary distance. Importantly, we find that saccade rate undergoes smooth, slow fluctuations on the scale of seconds, and accounting for those rate fluctuations was crucial for revealing the true degree of saccade rhythmicity. Thus, exact saccade timing is determined by an interaction between the slow saccade-rate fluctuations and the more temporally-local rhythmic generator. This demonstration of rhythmicity in overt oculomotor sampling behavior provides a link to the fundamentally rhythmic nature of many central perceptual and cognitive processes, and places primate saccadic sampling into the large family of rhythmic active sampling behaviors.

candidates.title: EPHB2 promotes long-range axon extension and its variants cause callosal dysgenesis
candidates.abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres, essential for integrating neural activity across large-scale brain networks. Accordingly, abnormal CC development is associated with diverse neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Callosal projection neurons (CPNs) of the cortex form the CC by extending long-range axons to the contralateral hemisphere; however, the mechanisms that sustain axon elongation over such remarkable distances remain poorly understood. Here we show that variants in the human gene EPHB2, which encodes a tyrosine kinase receptor regulating nervous system development and implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, cause CC dysgenesis. We characterise variant- specific effects on EPHB2 signalling and demonstrate that variants identified in individuals with distinct CC morphologies differentially alter CPN axon outgrowth and integration in vivo. We further show that EphB2 has a cell-autonomous, ligand-independent function in promoting CPN axon outgrowth by spatially organising actomyosin at axonal growth cones. These findings reveal a previously unrecognised role for EphB2 in promoting long-range axon extension and provide the first evidence that EPHB2 variants cause CC dysgenesis in humans. More broadly, our study links molecular variation in EPHB2 to individualised abnormalities in brain connectivity and provides a framework for understanding how heterogeneous circuit-level phenotypes arise in neurodevelopmental disorders.

candidates.title: Mathematical model for visual cortical development based on molecular mechanisms underlying the generation and elimination of dendritic spines
candidates.abstract: In the developing brain, neural circuits are elaborated by the activity-dependent rewiring of synaptic connections. The current view of synaptic rewiring in early development is that filopodia spontaneously generated along dendrites transform into spines by establishing contacts with neighboring axonal boutons to form synapses whereas spines of inappropriate synapses are eliminated in an activity-dependent manner. In this theoretical study, we mainly focus on the processes of spine generation, maturation, and elimination to build a mathematical model of synaptic rewiring, incorporating experimental findings on actin polymerization and depolymerization under the activation of Rho-GTPases mediated by the binding of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) to neurotrophin receptors such as tropomyosin kinase receptor B (TrkB) and the low-affinity-nerve growth factor receptor (p75NTR). TrkB receptors are dephosphorylated by chondroitin sulphate proteoglycans (CSPGs) mediated by protein-tyrosine phosphatase {sigma} (PTP{sigma} in an age-dependent manner. The model describes the generation or elimination of dendritic spines of visual cortical neurons under actin polymerization and depolymerization to establish appropriate synaptic contacts on afferent fibers of cells in the lateral geniculate nucleus. The simulations based on the model reproduced not only simple-cell-like receptive fields and orientation-direction maps but also a characteristic profile of the total number of synapses, which shows an early increase and a delayed decrease during the critical period. It is also demonstrated that the formation of direction selectivity is delayed behind the formation of orientation selectivity, which is likely promoted by the pruning of inappropriate synapses.

candidates.title: Polaris: A toolkit for standardized construction, integration, and quantitative testing in Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
candidates.abstract: Existing synthetic biology toolkits have expanded part libraries and assembly capabilities. However, new users may still encounter ambiguity in construct definitions, hierarchical transitions, genomic integration routes, and quantitative testing procedures. Here, we present Polaris, a Golden Gate toolkit for Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Polaris uses a MoClo-derived three-level hierarchy. Level 1 stores reusable parts, Level 2 generates transcription units and other intermediate constructs, and Level 3 supports multigene assembly and switching between testing and integration backbones. The toolkit distinguishes part interfaces from transcription unit interfaces, uses BpiI and BsaI in successive assembly stages, and provides parallel ccdB and mScarletI3 screening options. Integration modules and quantitative characterization frameworks were implemented in both hosts and demonstrated using representative genetic parts and activation and repression systems. A companion digital platform further encodes the Level 1 to Level 3 rules for assembly planning. Polaris connects hierarchical construction, stable genetic implementation, and quantitative testing within a common execution framework, providing a practical basis for data accumulation, part standardization, and future automation.

candidates.title: Scar Treatments in Hand Surgery.
candidates.abstract: Scar formation after hand surgery poses unique functional and aesthetic challenges because of the hand's complex anatomy, dense sensory innervation, and reliance on supple skin and tendon glide. Hypertrophic scars, keloids, adherent scars, and contractures can cause pain, hypersensitivity, restricted motion, and impaired activities of daily living, yet evidence guiding scar management in hand surgery remains limited and largely extrapolated from burn and general surgical populations. This review synthesizes current evidence on the biology, classification, prevention, and treatment of scars as they pertain to hand surgery. Nonoperative management, including silicone gel sheeting, compression therapy, intralesional corticosteroid injection, laser therapy, and hand therapy, forms the foundation of care. Operative interventions, ranging from scar excision and Z-plasty to skin grafting, local flap reconstruction, dermal substitutes, and tenolysis, address established contracture and adhesion when conservative measures fail. Emerging therapies, such as autologous fat grafting, growth factor modulation, platelet-rich plasma, and botulinum toxin A, show early promise but require validation in hand-specific trials. Optimal outcomes depend on a collaborative, individualized approach integrating patient risk stratification, meticulous surgical technique, and close coordination with hand therapy throughout the care continuum.
candidates.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online

candidates.title: Unsolved problems with ENaC: From molecules to mammals.
candidates.abstract: The epithelial Na channel (ENaC) mediates transport of Na+ in the kidney, the colon, the lung, and the sweat and salivary ducts. The activity of these channels is highly regulated and contributes to the maintenance of total body Na+, extracellular fluid volume, and plasma K+. Defects in the channel itself or in its regulation are implicated in hypertension and in other diseases. Despite progress in revealing many aspects of ENaC biology, many important questions remain unanswered. These include the following: What determines the remarkable ion selectivity of the channel? How is the channel directed to the apical plasma membrane? How does aldosterone regulate the channel? What is its role in producing urine with minimal Na+? And to what extent does the channel contribute to essential hypertension, cystic fibrosis, nephrotic syndrome, and liver failure? Here, I will discuss these questions and how they relate to our current understanding of the roles of ENaC in health and disease.

candidates.title: Genetic and environmental predictors of seasonality and seasonal affective disorder in individuals with depression.
candidates.abstract: The etiology and nosological status of seasonal affective disorder (SAD) as a specifier of depressive episodes versus a transdiagnostic disorder are the subject of debate. In this study, we investigated the underlying etiology of SAD and dimensional seasonality by examining their association with latitude and genetic risk for a range of traits, and investigated gene-environment interactions. This study included 12,460 adults (76% female, aged 18-90) with a history of depression from the Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Regression models included predictors for latitude (distance from equator) and polygenic scores for eight traits: major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, anxiety disorders, chronotype, sleep duration, body mass index, vitamin D levels, and educational attainment. Outcomes were SAD status and general seasonality score. SAD was positively associated with latitude (OR[95%CI] = 1.05[1.03-1.06], padjusted < 0.001), and there was nominal evidence of additive and multiplicative interactions between chronotype genetic risk and latitude (β = -0.0014[-0.0024,-0.0003], padjusted = 0.122; OR = 0.98[0.97-1.00], padjusted = 0.122). General seasonality score was associated with latitude (IRR = 1.01[1.01-1.01], padjusted < 0.001) and genetic risk for major depressive disorder (IRR =1.03[1.02-1.04], padjusted < 0.001), bipolar disorder (IRR = 1.02[1.01-1.03], padjusted = 0.001), anxiety disorders (IRR = 1.03[1.01-1.04], padjusted < 0.001), vitamin D levels (OR = 0.89[0.83-0.96], padjusted = 0.048), and educational attainment (IRR = 0.97[0.96-0.98], padjusted < 0.001). These findings enhance understanding of SAD etiology, highlighting contributions of psychiatric genetic risk and geographic measures on seasonal behavior, and support examining seasonality as a continuous dimension.

candidates.title: Characterizing hypertension in activated PI3K delta syndrome: Findings from Epic Cosmos.
candidates.abstract: APDS is a rare inborn error of immunity with comorbidity patterns that have yet to be characterized at a large scale. Using Epic Cosmos, a de-identified electronic health record database, we conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of 866 patients identified by structured diagnosis codes (ICD-10: D84.81; SNOMED: 793412000). Findings revealed that hypertension was coded as affecting 28.5% of the cohort, with age-stratified analyses demonstrating higher prevalence among younger APDS patients compared with age-matched non-APDS peers. Among patients aged ≤50 years, hypertension prevalence was 24.05% in the APDS group compared with 10.89% in the age-matched non-APDS population (prevalence ratio 2.21, 95% CI, 1.90-2.57, P < 0.0001). This association remained prominent in a more specific APDS sensitivity cohort in which the base population required an APDS diagnosis, alongside an allergy and immunology encounter. The findings of this paper provide large-scale characterization of APDS and identify hypertension, particularly among younger APDS patients, as a potentially underrecognized comorbidity that warrants further investigation.

candidates.title: Getting by "With a Little Help From My Friends": Collegial and peer support in allergy-immunology.
candidates.abstract: Health care professionals face many challenges in practice for which collegial and peer support can be impactful. Some of the most seemingly insurmountable struggles result from medical error or an adverse patient outcome. Clinicians may experience remorse, guilt, sadness, burnout, depression, and isolation, potentially causing second victim syndrome. In addition, medical professionals face daily frustrations due to loss of clinical autonomy, operational pressures, shrinking margins, workforce shortages, misaligned institutional incentives, and corporatization of health systems that can lead to burnout and moral injury. It is therefore critically important to support clinicians and ensure that those who dedicate their lives to caring for others feel heard, have a safe and supportive sounding board to debrief stressful situations, and do not feel abandoned. Collegial networks and peer support are important and helpful resources. This article reviews key aspects of collegial and peer support programs that can benefit health care professionals in allergy-immunology and beyond.
candidates.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. Global

candidates.title: Reprogramming tumor vasculature: Integrating normalization biology with vascularized tumor-on-chip models.
candidates.abstract: Abnormal tumor vasculature is a hallmark of the tumor microenvironment that promotes hypoxia, therapeutic resistance, and disease progression while limiting the delivery of anticancer therapy. Although early anti-angiogenic therapies were designed to starve tumors by eliminating their blood supply, excessive vessel pruning often aggravated hypoxia and selected for more aggressive phenotypes. These observations led to the concept of vascular normalization, whereby judicious modulation of angiogenic signaling transiently restores vessel structure and function, improving perfusion, oxygenation, drug delivery, and anti-tumor immunity. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms governing tumor vessel formation, maturation, and dysfunction, and examine therapeutic strategies aimed at normalizing the tumor vasculature. We further highlight the major challenges limiting clinical translation, including the transient and heterogeneous nature of the normalization window, adaptive resistance mechanisms, and the lack of robust tools for longitudinal monitoring. We then integrate vascular normalization biology with vascularized tumor-on-chip platforms, examining how key features of the tumor microenvironment, including tissue architecture, extracellular matrix remodeling, hemodynamic forces, metabolic gradients, and multicellular interactions, can be recreated and quantitatively monitored. We critically evaluate how engineering design, biomaterial selection, vascularization strategies, perfusion, and integrated sensing influence the ability of these platforms to capture vascular normalization and therapeutic responses. By linking the hallmarks of vascular normalization to measurable on-chip phenotypes, vascularized tumor-on-chip systems provide controlled frameworks for investigating resistance mechanisms, optimizing treatment timing, and advancing precision oncology. However, challenges related to physiological fidelity, standardization, scalability, and clinical validation continue to limit their broader translation.

candidates.title: Plug-and-Play or Plug-and-Pray? Impact of random versus targeted integration on the linearity and orthogonality of synthetic gene circuits in CHO cells.
candidates.abstract: Predictable and tuneable gene expression is essential for advanced mammalian cell engineering yet remains challenged by genomic position effects and copy number variability. This study systematically compares random integration (RI) and targeted integration (TI) of two synthetic lineariser gene circuits, TetR/eGFP_Lin and PhlFd/mCherry_Lin, in CHO-S cells. Both circuits exhibited strong linearity and orthogonality across integration strategies, but integration method and repressor choice produced distinct performance trade-offs. RI increased achievable dynamic range for PhlFd but increased basal leakiness for TetR, whereas TI, via a dual-landing-pad system, constrained copy number, and reduced basal expression and PhlFd expression variability. These findings highlight integration context and circuit architecture as key design parameters informing rational design of synthetic regulators for biopharmaceutical applications.

candidates.title: Enzymatic cross-linking collagen-based bioink for 3D bioprinting of endometrial model with endometrial epithelial organoids.
candidates.abstract: The human endometrium, a dynamic tissue responsive to sex hormones, plays a pivotal role in female reproduction and menstrual cycling, comprising diverse cell populations including epithelial and stromal cells. The development of in vitro endometrial models holds substantial potential for tissue repair, drug discovery, and disease modeling. However, the construction of biomimetic structural in vitro models capable of supporting long-term culture and preserving relevant biological functions has been hindered by limitations in both material properties and fabrication strategies. Here, an enzymatically cross-linked collagen-based bioink was developed, enabling extrusion bioprinting with favorable printability, biocompatibility, and bioactivity. The enzyme-catalyzed cross-linking process was optimized through room-temperature pre-crosslinking, and its evolution was described using a storage modulus (G')-time kinetic model, enabling prediction of the printable window and reliable fabrication of three-dimensional (3D) constructs. Then, monoculture and co-culture systems of endometrial epithelial organoids (EEOs) and endometrial stromal cells (ESCs) embedded in collagen-based hydrogels were established. Utilizing the bioink and printing strategy, an in vitro endometrial model was 3D bioprinted, exhibiting sustained viability (≥11 days) and hormone-responsive functions comparable to or showing enhanced functional characteristics relative to commonly used Matrigel-based or collagen-based systems. This biomimetic platform provides a physiologically relevant in vitro model for investigating endometrial biology, elucidating pathological mechanisms, and facilitating drug screening applications.
